overview.description: Gou Ji (often transliterated as Gao Ji) is a massive, chaotic, and highly strategic climbing card game from Shandong Province, China. It is famous for using four full decks of cards mixed together (216 cards total) and is played by six players divided into two teams of three. The name 'Gou Ji' means 'Enough Level' or 'Sufficient Rank', referring to the special high-ranking combinations that trigger 'Duels' between opposing players. It is a game of chaotic bursts of action, intricate teamwork, and psychological warfare.

history.origins: Originating in Qingdao, Shandong in the 1960s, Gou Ji became a cultural phenomenon in Northern China. It was developed to accommodate large groups of players with a surplus of cards.
timeline: 1980s: Spread across Shandong and Northern China.
1990s: Televised Gou Ji tournaments become popular in China.
Present: A staple of Chinese card gaming culture, with dedicated apps and professional leagues.
history.evolution: The game evolved from standard climbing games (like Zheng Shangyou) but added the unique 'Head-to-Head' (Duel) mechanic to allow cross-table interaction.
history.cultural: In Shandong, Gou Ji is more than a game; it is a social event. The ability to 'Gou Ji'â€”to interrupt play with a powerful handâ€”is seen as a sign of boldness and strength.

setup.players: 6 players. Seated alternating (Team A: 1, 3, 5; Team B: 2, 4, 6).
setup.deck: 4 decks of 52 cards + 8 Jokers (4 Red, 4 Black). Total 216 cards.
setup.dealing: Cards are dealt until the deck is exhausted (36 cards per player).

rules.objective: Be the first team to empty your hands. Points are awarded based on the finishing order (1st to 6th).
rules.gameplay: Gou Ji (Gao Ji) proceeds through deal, legal play actions, and end-of-round resolution. Play proceeds through legal actions until round resolution.
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Gou Ji (Gao Ji).
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: Scoring summary: Teams compete to finish 1st, 2nd, 3rd (Grand Slam).
Winning condition: Be the first team to empty your hands.

strategy.basic: Save your Gou Ji cards (High pairs, 2s, Jokers) to interrupt the game and force your rival to burn their cards. The goal is to 'suppress' your Dui Men.
strategy.intermediate: Help your partners. Since you can beat any non-Gou Ji play, if your partner plays a low hand (like a pair of 4s) and your right-hand opponent tries to beat it with a pair of 9s, you can slam a pair of Kings to win the trick and let your partner lead again.
strategy.advanced: The 'Shao Pai' Trap: Sometimes you should deliberately play a slightly weak Gou Ji (like 4 Jacks) to tempt your rival into wasting their Queens. Once their Queens are gone, your Kings become unstoppable.
tips: Never waste a Joker on a small hand unless it saves you from losing the lead.
Communicate with your team through your discards. Playing a single 3 usually means 'I have nothing, help me'.

difficulty.easy: Plays high cards randomly; fails to protect partners; uses Jokers on single 3s.
difficulty.medium: Recognizes Gou Ji thresholds (knows 2 Aces > 1 Ace); targets the direct rival (Dui Men) consistently.
difficulty.hard: Tracks all 8 Jokers and 16 Twos; calculates the 'Burn' probability before playing a Shao Pai; coordinates pushes to ensure the team finishes 1-2-3 (a 'Grand Slam').

considerations: AI must understand the 'Spatial' aspect of the tableâ€”it can only Gou Ji specific people.

phases.label: Deal
phases.notes: Players draw cards from the mixed 216-card deck until each has 36 cards.

phases.label: Climbing and Gou Ji Duels
phases.notes: Players beat singles or equal-size sets with higher rank sets. High enough sets trigger Gou Ji duels against opposite player.

phases.label: Scoring
phases.notes: Rank players by finish order and apply team score (+4,+2,0,0,-2,-4 with doubled 12-point swing for 1-2-3 sweep).

ante.reason: Gou Ji has no ante or stake-posting phase.

deal.description: Distribute 36 cards to each player from four combined decks and jokers.
deal.constraints: Dealer-driven deal at hand start; all cards are dealt out.

reveal_market.reason: There is no market reveal mechanic in Gou Ji.

buy_market.reason: Cards are never purchased from a market.

buy_stock.reason: Players do not buy cards from stock in this game.

fold.reason: Players stay active until they finish; no fold action exists.

check.reason: No betting rounds exist where checking applies.

call.reason: The rules contain no call or wager-matching action.

bet.reason: Gou Ji scoring is rank-based, not bet-based.

raise.reason: There is no raise action in this climbing game.

declare.reason: Special cases are handled by card play, not declaration actions.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands are private except optional teammate sharing conventions.

award_pot.description: Assign finish-order points to teams and apply sweep bonus scoring.
award_pot.constraints: System action after final placement is known.

play_card.description: Play a single card or equal-rank set that legally beats the previous play.
play_card.constraints: Must beat previous combination with same count; Gou Ji triggers duel behavior against opposite seat.

draw.reason: No draw phase exists because all cards are dealt initially.

discard.reason: Cards leave hand only by being played to the table.

pass.constraints: A passing player cannot re-enter the current trick cycle until cards clear.

bid.reason: Gou Ji does not use a bidding system.

meld.reason: The game uses climbing sets, not lasting meld groups.

go_out.description: Finish by playing your final legal set or single.
go_out.constraints: Player remains eligible to have final play beaten before wind-catching progression resumes.

wildcards.restrictions: Functions as wild in set construction and matching counts.
Can be beaten only by higher set containing sufficient red jokers.
Highest wild card and often creates unbeatable sets.

customLogicNeeded: Implement Gou Ji duel interruption against opposite seat only.
Support Shao Pai intervention and failure handling.
Apply tribute and liberation rules between hands in ordinary games.

engine.deckDescription: Four standard 52-card packs plus eight jokers shuffled together for a total of 216 cards used in Gou Ji.
engine.suitDescription: French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) are present but generally irrelevant in climbing and duel play.
engine.rankDescription: Order from high to low: Red Joker, Black Joker, then 2, A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3.
engine.dealPattern: Players draw cards in counterclockwise order until each has 36 cards.

synthesis.shortDescription: A massive and chaotic team-based climbing game from Shandong, China, using four full decks where powerful card combinations trigger one-on-one duels.

prompts.human: Welcome to Gou Ji, the epic Chinese card game. You're on a team of three playing against another team. Climb by playing card combinations. But beware: powerful combinations (Gou Ji) trigger duels with your direct rival. First team to empty their hands wins. Points: 1st=4, 2nd=2, 3rd-4th=0, 5th=-2, 6th=-4.
prompts.ai: Game: Gou Ji (Team climbing with duels). Players: 6 (2 teams of 3). Deck: 4Ã—52 cards + 8 Jokers (216 total). Deal: 36 cards per player. Card rank: Red Joker > Black Joker > 2 > A > K > Q > J > 10 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 6 > 5 > 4 > 3. Play: Combinations of same rank. Gou Ji (powerful combos): 5+ tens, 4+ jacks, 3+ queens, 2+ kings, 2+ aces, 1+ joker. Duel: When Gou Ji played, only direct opposite rival can beat it. Scoring: Finishing order determines points. Tribute: Losers give high cards to winners for next round.

scoring.description: Team scores follow finish order: 1st +4, 2nd +2, 3rd and 4th 0, 5th -2, 6th -4. If one team takes 1st-2nd-3rd, this 6-point swing doubles to 12.
scoring.winCondition: Teams play repeated hands and compare cumulative team points; higher score wins the session.

nullReasons.targetScore: Gou Ji sessions are commonly played to an agreed duration or stake settlement; 100 is a conventional session threshold that tables may adjust.
